text: True or False: The absence of any practical optical SRAM or DRAM — no way to store weights or activations in light — is described as one of the field's deepest limitations, keeping memory firmly in the electronic domain.
explanation: True — the book calls the lack of photonic memory the field's deepest limitation; weights and activations must live in electronic SRAM/DRAM, and DRAM access alone costs about 1 nJ per 64-bit word. Memory is a task where electronics wins decisively.
